summary: On steps with eflag==0 && vflag==0, pair table/rx/kk writes uCG/uCGnew on the device but marks only F_MASK modified, so the device updates are silently discarded by the next host sync.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:670-671 `if (eflag || vflag) atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify); else atomKK->modified(execution_space,F_MASK);` while the kernel writes uCG/uCGnew unconditionally: lines 527-531 `uCG_i += 0.5*evdwlOld; if (do_half) uCG(j) += ...; uCGnew_i += 0.5*evdwl; ...` and lines 546-547 `uCG(i) += uCG_i; uCGnew(i) += uCGnew_i;` (no EVFLAG guard). The two sibling RX pair styles get it right: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:151-152 and src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:238-239 both keep `UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK` in the `else` branch.
failure_scenario: A normal MD step (no thermo/dump output, eflag=vflag=0) with `pair_style table/rx/kk` + `fix eos/table/rx/kk`: the fix does `atomKK->sync(Host,UCG_MASK|UCGNEW_MASK)` (src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:290) which is a no-op because the dual view was never marked device-modified, then `modified(Host,...)` (line 292) and `sync(execution_space,...)` (line 294) copy the stale host values back over the device -> the pair style's uCG/uCGnew contributions are lost and the internal-energy/reaction integration is wrong on every non-output step.
suggested_fix: Change the else branch to `atomKK->modified(execution_space, F_MASK | UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK);`, matching pair_exp6_rx_kokkos and pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.

summary: The special-bond LJ weights are stored in a `Few<int,4>`, truncating fractional special_bonds factors (0.5 -> 0) and dropping those pair interactions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:679-683 `Few<int, 4> special_lj_local; special_lj_local[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ... special_lj_local[3] = force->special_lj[3];` (force->special_lj is `double[4]`, src/force.h:116). The functor signature keeps the int type (line 425 `Few<int, 4> const& special_lj`, line 570) and line 477 reads it: `const KK_FLOAT factor_lj = special_lj[sbmask(j)];`. The CPU base uses the double array directly: src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:94 `double *special_lj = force->special_lj;` and line 144 `factor_lj = special_lj[sbmask(j)];`.
failure_scenario: `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5` with `pair_style table/rx/kk`: 1-4 pairs get factor_lj = int(0.5) = 0 instead of 0.5, so those tabulated interactions (force, energy and the uCG/uCGnew contributions, all of which are multiplied by factor_lj) vanish. Silent wrong answer vs. the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Change `Few<int, 4>` to `Few<KK_FLOAT, 4>` (or `Few<double,4>`) in the local variable at line 679 and in the `compute_item`/`compute_all_items` signatures (lines 425, 570).

summary: PairTableRXKokkos::settings() releases the cutsq/tabindex dual views without freeing the aliased legacy row-pointer arrays, leaking them and leaving `cutsq`/`tabindex` dangling.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:1038-1047 `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); d_table_const.tabindex = d_table->tabindex = typename ArrayTypes<DeviceType>::t_int_2d_lr(); h_table->tabindex = ...; d_table_const.cutsq = d_table->cutsq = ...; h_table->cutsq = ...; allocated = 0; }`. Those arrays came from `memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,h_table->cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,...)` (line 985), which smallocs an nt-entry row-pointer array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:186-196) freed only by `destroy_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&)`. The CPU base frees them: src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:286-290 `memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); memory->destroy(tabindex);`.
failure_scenario: Repeated `pair_style table/rx/kk ...` commands leak the row-pointer arrays and leave `cutsq`/`tabindex` non-null but pointing into released view memory.
suggested_fix: Use `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,cutsq);` and `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->tabindex,tabindex);` instead of the manual view resets.

summary: getMixingWeights asserts `isite1 >= 0` / `isite2 >= 0`, which is false for the legal `1fluid` setting (OneFluidValue == -1), so debug builds abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:90-93 `assert(isite1 >= 0); assert(isite1 < nspecies); assert(isite2 >= 0); assert(isite2 < nspecies);` but line 50 `#define OneFluidValue (-1)` and lines 94/103/113 explicitly handle `isOneFluid(isite1)`; isite1/isite2 are set to OneFluidValue at lines 1161/1171 when the pair_coeff site name is "1fluid". The CPU base (src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:504-593) has no such assertion.
failure_scenario: `pair_coeff 1 1 table file.table ENTRY 1fluid 1fluid` in a build without NDEBUG (any Debug/RelWithDebInfo-without-NDEBUG build, host or CUDA) aborts inside the kernel at the first timestep.
suggested_fix: Drop the two lower-bound asserts, or relax them to `assert(isOneFluid(isite1) || (isite1 >= 0 && isite1 < nspecies));`.

summary: Global vdW energy is accumulated under `if (eflag)` rather than `if (eflag_global)`, polluting eng_vdwl on per-atom-energy-only steps.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:810 `if (eflag) eng_vdwl += static_cast<double>(ev.evdwl);` while line 811 uses `if (vflag_global)`. `ev.evdwl` is accumulated unconditionally in the kernel (line 534) and Pair::ev_setup only zeroes eng_vdwl when eflag_global is set.
failure_scenario: A step where only `compute pe/atom` runs (eflag==2, eflag_global==0) adds the whole pair energy into eng_vdwl without a reset.
suggested_fix: Use `if (eflag_global) eng_vdwl += ...`.

summary: On steps with eflag==0 && vflag==0 the style claims only F_MASK as modified, although the kernel writes uCG/uCGnew unconditionally. The next host sync therefore discards those device updates. Both sibling RX pair styles keep UCG_MASK|UCGNEW_MASK in the same else branch.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:669-670 'else atomKK->modified(execution_space,F_MASK);' vs src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:152 and src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:239, both 'F_MASK | UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK').

summary: min_post_force applies the SHAKE restraint force to the closest-image (possibly ghost) atom index instead of the mapped-back owner, and the following comm->reverse_comm(this) is a no-op, so ghost force contributions are silently dropped while the matching energy/virial are tallied on the owners.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:527-544 'const int idx0 = d_closest_list(i, slot0); const int idx1 = d_closest_list(i, slot1); ... a_f(idx0,0) += ...; a_f(idx1,0) -= ...' - no 'idx < nlocal' guard and no map-back.  The CPU original, RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:2842-2870 (FixShake::bond_force), first maps the image index back to the canonical owned index ('i1 = atom->map(atom->tag[i1]); i2 = atom->map(atom->tag[i2]);') and only then applies 'if ((i1 >= 0) && (i1 < nlocal)) f[i1][0] += delx*fbond;'.  The Kokkos code does perform that map-back a few lines later, but only for the energy/virial atom list (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:553-558 'own0 = AtomKokkos::map_kokkos<...>(d_shake_atom(m,slot0),...); if ((own0 >= 0) && (own0 < nlocal)) atomlist[count++] = own0;').  The 'comm->reverse_comm(this)' at fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:473 cannot recover the ghost forces: FixShake sets only 'comm_forward = 3' (RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:95) and never sets comm_reverse nor overrides pack_reverse_comm/unpack_reverse_comm (grep finds none in fix_shake.cpp/.h or fix_shake_kokkos.cpp/.h), and CommBrick::reverse_comm(Fix*,int) uses 'nsize = fix->comm_reverse' (comm_brick.cpp:1126-1127) which is 0.
failure_scenario: minimize with 'fix shake/kk' on a molecule that straddles a periodic boundary (so domain->closest_image returns a ghost index for a cluster partner owned by the same processor).  The restraint force on the ghost slot is thrown away, while ebond/virial/eatom are still credited to both owners: the reported SHAKE restraint energy and global virial are then twice the force that is actually applied, and the minimizer's forces differ by a factor of two from the plain 'fix shake' run.
suggested_fix: Map idx0/idx1 back through the atom map (as done for own0/own1 at lines 553-558) and guard the force accumulation with '< nlocal', exactly as FixShake::bond_force does; then drop the dead comm->reverse_comm(this) call at line 473 (or add a real pack/unpack_reverse_comm and set comm_reverse).

summary: The d_b_stats/d_a_stats bond/angle statistics that min_post_force allocates, zeroes and accumulates with atomics every minimization step are never copied to the host, never MPI-reduced and never printed - the work and the per-step device allocation are entirely wasted.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:433-446 allocate and zero 'd_b_stats'/'d_a_stats' on every min_post_force call; lines 577-581 and 608-611 accumulate into them with Kokkos::atomic_add/max/min.  'grep -n "[db]_[ba]_stats" src/KOKKOS/fix_shake_kokkos.{cpp,h}' shows no other use: no deep_copy back to the host, no MPI_Allreduce, no output.  The CPU original does the reduce and the printing inline in min_post_force (RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:996-1031).  The Kokkos version instead prints via FixShake::stats() (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:504-507), which recomputes the statistics from the current coordinates, so the accumulators are pure dead code.  A related inconsistency inside the dead block: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:607-612 updates a_max/a_min only 'if (count > 0)', whereas RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:988-989 updates them unconditionally.
failure_scenario: any 'minimize' with 'fix shake/kk ... output_every > 0': two extra device allocations plus a full atomic scatter per step whose result is discarded.
suggested_fix: Either copy d_b_stats/d_a_stats back to b_count/b_ave/b_max/b_min and reduce+print them as FixShake::min_post_force does, or delete the accumulators and the zeroing kernel and keep only the FixShake::stats() call.

summary: min_post_force marks x as modified on the device before calling stats(), although the kernel never writes x; this can force a spurious device->host copy of the coordinates or collide with a pending host-side modification.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:504-507 'if (update->ntimestep == next_output) { atomKK->modified(execution_space, X_MASK); stats(); }'.  The min_post_force kernel (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:515-615) only reads d_x and writes d_f; the datamask sync at line 386 is 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, X_MASK | F_MASK)'.  FixShakeKokkos::stats() already does 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK)' (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp, stats()), so the modified() call is not needed to get x onto the host.
failure_scenario: a minimization step in which the host copy of x is the current one (host modify flag set) and this call also sets the device modify flag, leaving both sides claimed for k_x.
suggested_fix: Remove the 'atomKK->modified(execution_space, X_MASK);' call; stats() already syncs x to the host.

summary: pack_forward_comm_kokkos and unpack_forward_comm_kokkos launch Kokkos::parallel_for with '*this' as the functor without setting copymode = 1, so the functor copy's destructor is only harmless because post_force() happens to have set copymode earlier.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2130-2133 'if (pbc_flag) Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagFixShakePackForwardComm<1>...,*this); else Kokkos::parallel_for(...<0>...,*this);' and fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2178 'Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagFixShakeUnpackForwardComm>(0,n),*this);' - neither is bracketed by 'copymode = 1; ... copymode = 0;'.  Every other parallel_for(*this) in the file does bracket it (lines 262-266, 430-463, 633-740, 1964-1969, 2052-2056), as do the sibling styles (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:497-501, fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:288-292).  Without the guard the copy's ~FixShakeKokkos would run with copymode == 0 and execute the full teardown, including 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_shake_atom,shake_atom)' which does 'sfree(array)' (KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:272-281) on the row pointers still owned by the original object.
failure_scenario: any future caller that invokes comm->forward_comm(this) outside FixShakeKokkos::post_force() (which sets copymode = 1 at line 633 before the forward comm at line 668) gets a double free of shake_atom/shake_type/closest_list plus a spurious bondtype_findset() pass over all local atoms.
suggested_fix: Set copymode = 1 before and copymode = 0 after the parallel_for in both pack_forward_comm_kokkos and unpack_forward_comm_kokkos.

summary: fix shake/kk reads per-type masses from atomKK->k_mass on the device but never syncs that DualView to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:638-639 and 864-865 `d_rmass = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>(); d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, used in the kernels at lines 908 (`dtfsq_kk / mass[type[i]]`), 972-973, 1098-1100, 1292-1295, 1545-1546 (`1.0/d_mass[d_type[i0]]`).  The file syncs many of its own DualViews (lines 192-193, 227-228, 255, 387-393) but `grep -n 'k_mass' fix_shake_kokkos.cpp` shows no `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`.  k_mass is host-only-written (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316, `modify_host()` only) and is not covered by any bit in src/atom_masks.h, so `atomKK->sync(execution_space,...)` cannot bring it over; cf. the required idiom in src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46.
failure_scenario: GPU run whose only k_mass sync came from another style: it works by accident.  Remove/replace that style (e.g. integrate with a non-KOKKOS-synced integrator, or run `fix shake` inside a minimisation) and d_mass is all zeros, so every SHAKE inverse mass is 1/0 = inf and constrained bond lengths blow up.  Any `mass` command issued between two runs also invalidates the device copy (modify_host) and nothing re-syncs it here.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: 13 of the 16 angle KOKKOS styles in this group have no `action` lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, contrary to KOKKOS rule 5.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:37-50 lists only angle_charmm, angle_class2, angle_cosine, angle_table, angle_harmonic, angle_hybrid and angle_spica. Missing: angle_class2_p6_kokkos.{cpp,h} (base src/MOFFF/angle_class2_p6.cpp), angle_class2xe_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/CLASS2/angle_class2xe.cpp), angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_periodic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cross_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/YAFF/angle_cross.cpp), angle_dipole_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/DIPOLE/angle_dipole.cpp), angle_fourier_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_gaussian_kokkos.{cpp,h}. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 requires an action line per new file, with the base file name as second argument when the base lives in an optional package.
failure_scenario: No build breakage today: KOKKOS's action() only does `rm -f ../$1` (install mode is refused outright at Install.sh:216) and CMake finds the files through RegisterStylesExt (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:304). The consequence is that `make no-kokkos`/`make purge` will not remove stale src/ copies of these files left over from an older tree, and the file list drifts out of sync with the documented convention.
suggested_fix: Add the 26 missing `action <file> <base file>` lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh in alphabetical order alongside the existing angle_* entries.

summary: angle_mm3_kokkos, angle_mwlc_kokkos and angle_quartic_kokkos have no action lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, so the traditional make build never installs them and the mm3/kk, mwlc/kk and quartic/kk styles silently do not exist there.
evidence: 'grep "^action angle" src/KOKKOS/Install.sh' returns only lines 37-50 (charmm, class2, cosine, table, harmonic, hybrid, spica). The files src/KOKKOS/angle_mm3_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_mwlc_kokkos.{cpp,h} and angle_quartic_kokkos.{cpp,h} exist and register AngleStyle(mm3/kk,...), AngleStyle(mwlc/kk,...), AngleStyle(quartic/kk,...) (angle_mm3_kokkos.h:16-18, angle_mwlc_kokkos.h:16-18, angle_quartic_kokkos.h:16-18). Their base classes live in optional packages (src/YAFF/angle_mm3.cpp, src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_mwlc.cpp, src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_quartic.cpp), so per .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 they need two-argument action lines, e.g. 'action angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp angle_mm3.cpp'.
failure_scenario: 'cd src && make yes-kokkos yes-yaff yes-extra-molecule && make mpi' produces a binary in which 'angle_style mm3/kk' fails with 'Unrecognized angle style'; a CMake build of the same tree has the style, so the two build systems disagree. (The same omission affects several other angle kk styles outside this review group.)
suggested_fix: Add the six missing action lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, each naming both the KOKKOS file and its package base file, and audit the rest of the angle_*_kokkos files for the same omission.

summary: Eleven newly added KOKKOS bond styles have no action lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, violating KOKKOS rule 5, so 'make no-kokkos' leaves stale copies of them in src/.
evidence: grep '^action bond_' src/KOKKOS/Install.sh returns only class2, fene, table, harmonic, hybrid and quartic_exp (lines 80-91). Missing: bond_fene_expand_kokkos, bond_fene_nm_kokkos, bond_gaussian_kokkos, bond_gromos_kokkos, bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos, bond_harmonic_shift_kokkos, bond_harmonic_shift_cut_kokkos, bond_mm3_kokkos, bond_morse_kokkos, bond_nonlinear_kokkos, bond_quartic_kokkos (.cpp and .h each). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 requires 'Register new files in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh with action lines', passing both filenames when the base class lives in an optional package (e.g. bond_gaussian.cpp is in EXTRA-MOLECULE, bond_mm3.cpp in YAFF).
failure_scenario: A tree that once had the KOKKOS package installed under the legacy make build, then 'make no-kokkos': the 22 unregistered files stay behind in src/ and are compiled into the next non-KOKKOS build, producing undefined KOKKOS symbols. (Impact is limited because src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:757 now aborts install mode - the package is CMake-only - so action() is used only for removal.)
suggested_fix: Add the missing 'action bond_<name>_kokkos.cpp bond_<name>.cpp' / '.h' pairs next to the existing bond entries at lines 80-91.

summary: dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos, dihedral_quadratic_kokkos and dihedral_spherical_kokkos (and ~42 other KOKKOS style files) have no `action` line in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, so a traditional-make `make yes-kokkos` build never installs them and the /kk styles are missing from lmp_serial/lmp_mpi.
evidence: `grep -n 'nharmonic\|quadratic\|spherical' src/KOKKOS/Install.sh` returns nothing, while the sibling styles are registered at src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:150-169 (`action dihedral_fourier_kokkos.cpp dihedral_fourier.cpp`, `action dihedral_table_kokkos.cpp dihedral_table.cpp`, `action dihedral_opls_kokkos.cpp dihedral_opls.cpp`, ...).  A full sweep (`for f in src/KOKKOS/*_kokkos.cpp; do grep -q "^action $(basename $f)" Install.sh || echo $f; done`) lists 45 unregistered files, among them dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_quadratic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_spherical_kokkos.{cpp,h}.  This violates rule 5 of .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md.
failure_scenario: `cd src && make yes-kokkos && make serial` then an input with `dihedral_style nharmonic/kk` -> "Unknown dihedral style" (the CMake build is unaffected because it globs the package directory, so CI does not catch this).
suggested_fix: Add the missing `action <file>_kokkos.cpp <base>.cpp` / `.h` lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh (base file name given because the bases live in EXTRA-MOLECULE), and audit the other 42 unregistered files at the same time.

summary: 45 style file pairs (90 files) added to src/KOKKOS after the legacy-build removal have no 'action' line in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, so 'make no-kokkos' / 'make purge' would leave stale copies of them in src/ for anyone who still has an old legacy-build tree.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/Install.sh contains 708 'action <file>' lines but src/KOKKOS holds 795 .cpp/.h files; the 90 with no action line are (as .cpp/.h pairs, 45 styles):
angle_class2_p6_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_class2xe_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_periodic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cross_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_dipole_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_fourier_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_gaussian_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_mm3_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_mwlc_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_quartic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_fene_expand_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_fene_nm_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_gaussian_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_gromos_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_harmonic_shift_cut_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_harmonic_shift_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_mm3_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_morse_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_nonlinear_kokkos.{cpp,h}, bond_quartic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_class2xe_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_helix_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_quadratic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_spherical_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_cossq_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_distance_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_distharm_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_fourier_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_inversion_harmonic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_ring_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.{cpp,h}, improper_umbrella_kokkos.{cpp,h}, pair_lj96_cut_kokkos.{cpp,h}, pair_lj_cubic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, tune_kokkos.{cpp,h}
The action() function itself is now uninstall-only -- src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:12-16:
  action () {
    if (test $mode = 0) then
      rm -f ../$1
    fi
  }
and src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:751-753 makes install/update abort:
  if (test $1 = 1 || test $1 = 2) then
    echo "The KOKKOS package no longer supports the legacy build system. Please build LAMMPS with CMake instead."
    exit 1
so the missing lines cannot break an install; they only mean the uninstall sweep is incomplete.  All 45 styles were added after the legacy install branch was deleted, so no src/ copy of them can exist today -- hence low severity.  (The two remaining rule-1 scan hits, src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:746-747 for mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx and mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx, are false positives: both .pyx files exist, as do their src/ML-IAP dependencies.)
failure_scenario: A developer with a working tree that predates the legacy-build removal and once ran 'make yes-kokkos' runs 'make no-kokkos' or 'make purge': the 90 listed files stay behind in src/, and a subsequent CMake configure fails with the 'make-generated header files found in src/' error, or a legacy 'make serial' silently compiles the leftover KOKKOS sources.
suggested_fix: Add the 90 missing 'action <file>' lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh (keeping the list alphabetical), or -- since action() is now purely a remove sweep -- replace the explicit list with a loop over the package directory contents.

summary: The per-atom virial array k_vatom is sized and size-checked with `maxeatom` instead of `maxvatom`, so when per-atom stress is requested without per-atom energy the array is never allocated and v_tally writes out of bounds / through a null pointer.
failure_scenario: `pair_style mliap/kk ...` plus `compute s all stress/atom NULL` and a dump of it, with no per-atom energy compute: eflag_atom stays 0 so maxeatom stays 0, the `extent(0) < maxeatom` test is 0 < 0 (false), k_vatom/vatom are never allocated, and the first v_tally dereferences a null `vatom` (host path) or writes past a zero-extent view (device path) - segfault or silent memory corruption.
suggested_fix: Use `maxvatom` in both the extent comparison and the create_kokkos call (and fix the "pair:eatom" memory label to "pair:vatom").

summary: The per-atom virial block sizes and size-checks k_vatom with maxeatom instead of maxvatom (and labels the allocation 'pair:eatom'). When per-atom stress is requested without per-atom energy, maxeatom stays 0, the test '0 < 0' is false, k_vatom/vatom are never allocated, and the first v_tally writes through a null pointer / a zero-extent view.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:99-108 vs the correct eatom block at :88-97; Pair::ev_setup only raises maxeatom under eflag_atom and maxvatom under vflag_atom).

summary: post_force syncs only X and MASK to the host before calling Group::xcm()/Group::mass(), but those routines also read atom->image, atom->type and atom->rmass, whose host copies are stale after DomainKokkos::pbc() marks IMAGE modified on the device - the unwrapped center of mass is then wrong by whole box lengths.
evidence: fix_spring_kokkos.cpp:67 'atomKK->sync(Host, X_MASK | MASK_MASK);' (and the identical line 126 in the COUPLE branch) immediately followed by 'if (group->dynamic[igroup]) masstotal = group->mass(igroup); group->xcm(igroup, masstotal, xcm);' (lines 69-70, 128-131).  src/group.cpp Group::xcm reads 'imageint *image = atom->image; ... domain->unmap(x[i], image[i], unwrap);' plus 'int *type = atom->type; double *mass = atom->mass; double *rmass = atom->rmass;'.  src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:398-430 (DomainKokkos::pbc) runs DomainPBCFunctor on the device over atomKK->k_image and ends with 'atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK|V_MASK|IMAGE_MASK);' - so the host image array is stale until something syncs IMAGE_MASK to the host.  Nothing does inside the run loop: VerletKokkos::run sets 'lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 0;' (verlet_kokkos.cpp:311) and only performs 'atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK)' on output timesteps (verlet_kokkos.cpp:547) and after the loop (:555).  Contrast the CPU FixSpring, which runs entirely on the host with always-current image flags.
failure_scenario: 'fix spring/kk tether' (or couple) on a group whose atoms cross a periodic boundary during the run: on every non-thermo timestep after a pbc remap, domain->unmap uses the pre-remap image flag with the post-remap coordinate, so xcm jumps by one box length, and the spring force k*(r-r0) applied to the whole group is grossly wrong (and espring / f_spring output with it).
suggested_fix: Change both syncs to 'atomKK->sync(Host, X_MASK | MASK_MASK | IMAGE_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK);' so every array Group::xcm()/Group::mass() touches is current on the host.

summary: post_force pulls the full coordinate array back to the host every timestep just to compute the group center of mass with the host-only Group::xcm(), which defeats most of the benefit of the device kernel.
evidence: fix_spring_kokkos.cpp:67 and :126 'atomKK->sync(Host, X_MASK | MASK_MASK);' followed by group->xcm(...) on lines 70 and 130-131; the force kernels at :113/:118/:184/:189 then run on the device.  Other KOKKOS fixes that need a group reduction do it with a device parallel_reduce instead (e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp), and .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md warns that forcing a full x transfer every step 'is slower than no /kk at all'.
failure_scenario: any GPU run with 'fix spring/kk': one device->host copy of x (3*nlocal doubles) per timestep, plus (if IMAGE_MASK is added per the sync bug above) the image array too.
suggested_fix: Compute the center of mass (and the dynamic-group mass) with a Kokkos::parallel_reduce over the device views followed by a single MPI_Allreduce, as fix_momentum_kokkos does.

summary: update_box() syncs x to the host BEFORE calling the base class and marks the host modified AFTER it, but the base class updates x on the DEVICE in between (DomainKokkos::x2lamda/lamda2x), so the trailing modified(Host,ALL_MASK) makes the stale pre-deform host coordinates newer than the remapped device coordinates and the next sync to device reverts every atom position.
failure_scenario: `fix deform ... remap x` (the default) together with any rigid fix (rfix is filled with every fix whose rigid_flag is set, src/fix_deform.cpp:693-696) in a KOKKOS GPU run: on every deform step the device receives the coordinates as they were before the affine remap, so atoms are not rescaled with the box, the system immediately develops overlaps/lost atoms and the trajectory is wrong. In a Kokkos debug build (KOKKOS_ENABLE_DEBUG_DUALVIEW_MODIFY_CHECK) it instead aborts with a concurrent host/device modification error.
suggested_fix: Drop the ALL_MASK bracket entirely (Fix::deform() only transforms the fix-owned xcm arrays, not per-atom data -- see src/RIGID/fix_rigid.cpp:1285-1293), or, if a host bracket is really wanted, narrow it to the fields the rigid fixes read and place the sync/modified pair around only the `ifix->deform()` loops rather than around the device x2lamda/lamda2x calls.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are declared int in NPairSSAKokkosExecute, truncating the half box lengths used by minimum_image_check().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:175 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' and constructor parameters :237 'const int & _xprd_half, const int & _yprd_half, const int & _zprd_half'; initialized from the doubles 'domain->xprd_half,domain->yprd_half,domain->zprd_half' at src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:428 (src/domain.h:50 declares them double).  Used in a floating point test at src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:342-347, which must match src/domain.h:198-204 as used by the CPU build at src/DPD-REACT/npair_half_bin_newton_ssa.cpp:211 and :296.
failure_scenario: Same as the npair_kokkos.h case: in a box whose half-length is not an integer, special-bond pairs whose |dx| falls between trunc(xprd_half) and xprd_half are stored without the special-bond code and lose their special_lj/special_coul scaling, so SSA/DPD runs disagree with the CPU build.
suggested_fix: Change the three members and the matching constructor parameters to double.

summary: The device kernel calls the host <cmath> function fmod() instead of Kokkos::fmod(), violating the KOKKOS rule that device kernels use Kokkos:: math functions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.cpp:186-187 inside the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION operator(): `sgn = (fmod(static_cast<double>(d_N[type]), 2.0) == 0.0) ? static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(-1.0) : static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0);`. Every other math call in the same kernel is namespace-qualified (`Kokkos::sqrt` :154, `Kokkos::acos` :169, `Kokkos::cos` :171, `Kokkos::sin` :178, `Kokkos::fabs` :177). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...), never std:: -- std::pow and friends fail to compile for GPU targets.' The CPU original is src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_fourier_simple.cpp:132 `sgn = (fmod(N[type], 2.0) == 0.0) ? -1.0 : 1.0;`.
failure_scenario: Backends that do not inject a __device__ overload of the unqualified ::fmod (SYCL/OpenMPTarget, or a build where <cmath> pulls in only the host overload) fail to compile angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.cpp. Where it does compile it forces a double-precision fmod inside an otherwise single-precision kernel.
suggested_fix: Replace `fmod(static_cast<double>(d_N[type]), 2.0)` with `Kokkos::fmod(d_N[type], static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(2.0))`.

summary: s_KK_double2, the reduction type used for every force dot product in the KOKKOS minimizers, stores its two accumulators as KK_FLOAT, which is 'float' in single- and mixed-precision builds, so the global sums lose precision even when the forces themselves are double.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.h:22-23 'struct s_KK_double2 { KK_FLOAT d0, d1;'.  src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:400-409 'typedef float KK_FLOAT; typedef float KK_ACC_FLOAT;' for LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and 'typedef float KK_FLOAT; typedef double KK_ACC_FLOAT;' for the mixed setting LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE.  It is used as the parallel_reduce value type over all local degrees of freedom in src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:288-303 (fh in linemin_quadratic), :444-459 (compute_dir_deriv) and src/KOKKOS/min_cg_kokkos.cpp:127-143 (the CG force tolerance and Polak-Ribiere beta), e.g. 'sdot.d0 += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(l_fvec[i]*l_fvec[i]);' where l_fvec is KK_ACC_FLOAT.  Every other reduction in the same files deliberately accumulates in double: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:193-195 'LAMMPS_LAMBDA(const int& i, double& fdothme)', :228-230, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:214-216, and min_kokkos.cpp:626-635/663-672/700-710.
failure_scenario: A mixed-precision KOKKOS build (the recommended GPU setting) with min_style cg/kk on a few hundred thousand atoms: dotall[0] and dotall[1] are float sums of ~10^6 terms, so beta = MAX(0.0,(dotall[0]-dotall[1])/gg) and the ftol test lose roughly all digits past 1e-7 relative, degrading or stalling convergence, while the same run in double precision converges.
suggested_fix: Declare d0 and d1 as double (the struct is already named double2) so the reduction accumulates in double regardless of the KK_FLOAT setting.

summary: The KOKKOS constructor frees the base class's storque array and sets the pointer to nullptr but never allocates the replacement dual view, so `storque` stays null until `atom->nmax > maxatom` first becomes true; the atom-style variable path then dereferences a null pointer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_atom_kokkos.cpp:115-116 `memory->destroy(storque); storque = nullptr;` -- no create_kokkos follows. src/GRANULAR/fix_addtorque_atom.cpp:99-100 leaves the base with `maxatom = 1; memory->create(storque, maxatom, 3, ...)`, and the KOKKOS class does not reset `maxatom`. The only allocation site is src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_atom_kokkos.cpp:169-174 `if (varflag == ATOM && atom->nmax > maxatom) { ... create_kokkos(k_storque,storque,maxatom,3,...) }`, which is skipped whenever `atom->nmax <= 1`. Line 193 then evaluates `&storque[0][0]`. The two sibling styles do it correctly: fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:125-127 and fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:43-44 both call `memory->destroy(sforce)` followed immediately by `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_sforce,sforce,maxatom,...)` in the constructor.
failure_scenario: A rank whose `atom->nmax` is still the 1 set by `AtomVec::grow(1)` in create_box.cpp:274 / atom.cpp:696 (a sub-domain that never owns or ghosts an atom) running `fix addtorque/atom/kk` with an atom-style variable: line 169's guard is false, `storque` is null, and `input->variable->compute_atom(xvar,igroup,&storque[0][0],3,0)` at line 193 dereferences null -> segfault. The plain CPU fix does not crash there because the base allocation survives.
suggested_fix: Follow fix_addforce_kokkos/fix_setforce_kokkos: in the constructor replace the base allocation with `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_storque,storque,maxatom,3,"addtorque/atom:storque"); d_storque = k_storque.view<DeviceType>();` right after `memory->destroy(storque)`.

summary: d_scale is declared as an integer view (AT::t_int_2d) but holds the MEAM `scale` factor, which is a double; every scale value is truncated to an integer on the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 `typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;` (and the same type in src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 and its meam_dens_final/meam_force signatures). It is filled in src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:299-310 from the CPU `double **scale`: `MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_scale,"pair:scale",n+1,n+1); ... h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j];`. The CPU base declares `double **scale` (src/MEAM/pair_meam.h) and uses it as a double: src/MEAM/meam_dens_final.cpp:34 `scaleii = scale[type[i]][type[i]];`, src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 `scaleij = scale[type[i]][type[j]];`.
failure_scenario: `fix adapt ... pair meam scale 1 1 v_ramp` with a scale that ramps 0->1: on the device every value below 1.0 truncates to 0 (energies/forces zeroed) and 1.5 truncates to 1, so pair meam/kk gives completely different energies from pair meam.
suggested_fix: Change d_scale to a floating-point view (`typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d`) in pair_meam_kokkos.h, meam_kokkos.h and the meam_dens_final/meam_force signatures.

summary: A std:: facility (std::numeric_limits<>::min()) is used inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION device kernel, which the KOKKOS package rules forbid and which only compiles with --expt-relaxed-constexpr.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:154 'static constexpr KK_ACC_FLOAT SMALL_KK = std::numeric_limits<KK_ACC_FLOAT>::min();' inside 'void BondGaussianKokkos<DeviceType>::operator()(TagBondGaussianCompute<NEWTON_BOND,EVFLAG>, const int &n, EV_FLOAT& ev) const' (:149). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ..., never std::'. Kokkos provides Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v / finite_min_v for this.
failure_scenario: Any nvcc/hipcc build without --expt-relaxed-constexpr (or a future toolchain that tightens constexpr host-function use in device code) fails to compile bond_gaussian_kokkos.cpp; today Kokkos enables the flag so it builds.
suggested_fix: Replace with a Kokkos-provided constant (Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v<KK_ACC_FLOAT>) or a literal guarded by an if constexpr on sizeof(KK_ACC_FLOAT).

summary: ModifyKokkos declares a member function pre_decide() that is never defined and never called, and it does not override anything in Modify.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.h:34 'void pre_decide();' -- it carries no 'override' (Modify has no such virtual, see src/modify.h:58-104) and 'grep -rn pre_decide src/' finds only this one line: there is no definition in src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp and no caller.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; any future call to it would be an undefined-reference link error rather than the intended behavior.
suggested_fix: Remove the declaration, or implement it if a pre-decide hook is actually wanted.

summary: The 'Loading python model complete' message is printed by every MPI rank because the comm->me == 0 guard of the CPU version was dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:129-130 'model_loaded = 1; utils::logmesg(MLIAPModelKokkos<DeviceType>::lmp, "Loading python model complete.\n");' versus src/ML-IAP/mliap_model_python.cpp:131-132 'model_loaded = 1; if (comm->me == 0) utils::logmesg(lmp, "Loading python model complete.\n");'. The deferred-load message a few lines above (mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:106-107) does keep the guard, so the omission is clearly unintended.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style mliap/kk model mliappy ...' on N MPI ranks prints the line N times into the screen/log output.
suggested_fix: Wrap the logmesg in 'if (MLIAPModelKokkos<DeviceType>::comm->me == 0)' like the CPU version and like the deferred-load branch above it.

summary: nm/cut/coul/long/kk silently ignores the tabulated Coulomb path (ncoultablebits / pair_modify table), so it does not reproduce the CPU style's numbers; it is the only KOKKOS coul/long style lacking the CoulLongTable specialisation.
evidence: KOKKOS compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul (src/KOKKOS/pair_nm_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp:190-208, 243-260) always evaluate the erfc polynomial and never consult rtable/ftable/ctable/etable; compute() dispatches with Specialisation=void (line 124: 'ev = pair_compute<PairNMCutCoulLongKokkos<DeviceType>,void>'). The CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_nm_cut_coul_long.cpp:134-157 branches on 'if (!ncoultablebits || rsq <= tabinnersq)' and otherwise interpolates the tables, and init_style (same file, line 316) still calls init_tables(cut_coul,nullptr). Every other KOKKOS coul/long style (pair_lj_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, pair_born_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, pair_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, ...) instantiates pair_compute<...,CoulLongTable<1>> and implements the table branch.
failure_scenario: Default settings (ncoultablebits=12): running the same input with 'pair_style nm/cut/coul/long' vs '.../kk' gives Coulomb forces/energies that differ by the table interpolation error (~1e-6 relative), and the tables allocated by init_tables() are dead memory.
suggested_fix: Add the CoulLongTable<1>/<0> specialisation branch to compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul and dispatch pair_compute with CoulLongTable<ncoultablebits?1:0> as in pair_lj_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, or at minimum force ncoultablebits=0 in the KOKKOS init_style so CPU and GPU agree.
